String Utilities Example

strutil.h, base 64 and CRC-32: the small helpers most programs need around a database, each checked against a known answer.

Contents

What It Shows
Running It
Sample Output
Source

What It Shows

  • strutil.h: trim, split, case changes, case-blind compare and find, starts_with and ends_with, replace_all, cutting around a marker, printf-style format(), number conversion that never throws, copy_to() into fixed char fields and natural ordering ("run2" before "run10").
  • gxs_b64.h: base 64 (RFC 4648) for binary data in text, with line breaks ignored and bad input refused, and HTTP basic authentication.
  • gxcrc32.h: CRC-32 of a buffer and of a file, computed in one call and block by block.

Running It

string_utils [file]            # with a file, also its CRC-32 two ways

Sample Output

strutil.h
  split + trim                       5 fields: AMTX|buy|100|3.25|opening flush
  copy_to(char[5], "TOOLONG")        "TOOL" (4 chars)
  natural_compare sort               run1.log run2.log run10.log
gxs_b64.h
  encode("foobar")                   Zm9vYmFy
  basic auth header                  Basic dHJhZGVyOnMzY3JldA==
gxcrc32.h
  CRC-32("123456789")                CBF43926
All checks pass

Source

examples/general/string_utils.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as string_utils and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
